title: Noise source mapping and metric rediscovery
content:
Purpose:
This is an experimental runbook + investigation log for a recurring category of noise: transient SLO burn alerts caused by missing or misaggregated metrics, combined with noisy downstream synthetic checks. Goal is to create a reproducible mapping from observed alert symptoms -> likely metric-level root causes -> short-term mitigations -> long-term fixes.

Summary of the problem we've seen (Dec 2025 -> Feb 2026 window):
- Multiple oncalls in region-us reported SLO burn alerts for api.latency.p95 in short bursts (5–15m) that resolved without deploys.
- Datadog synthetic checks and k8s probe flaps coincided in ~40% incidents.
- Investigation often found one of: (A) scrape hiccups from sidecar prometheus-exporter, (B) stale histogram bucket aggregation after service restart, (C) export queue backpressure causing drop of high-cardinality labels, (D) abrupt rollups in our metric-rollup lambda.
- Existing runbooks point to throttling/infra, but not to a structured fingerprinting approach.

What we tried (quick notes):
1) Fingerprint pipeline (proto):
   - Capture alert telemetry: alert_id, start_ts, end_ts, metric_name, tags, host_list, raw_timeseries_ids (where available)
   - Correlate with recent deploys, autoscaler events, node reboots, and exporter logs +/- 10m window
   - Compute feature vector: scrape_error_rate, missing_points_ratio, cardinality_delta, histogram_bucket_delta, synthetic_check_fail_rate
   - Cluster incidents with DBSCAN to find recurring fingerprints
   --> Early results: 3 dominant clusters accounting for ~65% incidents.

2) Quick probe queries (Prometheus / Datadog examples):
   - missing_points_ratio: 1 - (count_over_time(metric[10m]) / expected_points)
   - cardinality_delta: cardinality(metric{job=~".*"}, 10m) - cardinality(metric{job=~".*"}, 30m)
   - histogram_bucket_delta: sum(rate(my_histogram_bucket[5m])) by (le) - sum(rate(my_histogram_bucket[30m])) by (le)
   Use these as heuristics in the alert payload to reduce hand chase.

3) Short-term mitigations we've prototyped (fast ops playbook):
   - Auto-suppress SLO burn alerts if missing_points_ratio > 0.3 AND cardinality_delta < -0.5 for the same window (meaning missing series likely caused the spike). Suppression window: 10m, with notice to oncall to still investigate.
   - Add traceback link to exporter logs in the alert (if exporter label present) to speed root cause mapping.
   - Fallback rule: when histogram buckets show >90% of p95 mass in a single stale bucket, do not count that p95 toward rolling SLO until resolution.

Operational experiments to run (A/B style):
- Experiment A: alert suppression on 10 high-noise services for 4 weeks. Metric: number of actionable pages / week and mean time to detection of true regressions.
- Experiment B: keep current alerts + add extra diagnostic fields in payload (no suppression). Compare pages and time-to-ack.

Investigation playbook (detailed flow for oncall):
1) When an SLO burn alert fires, immediately collect: the alert payload, list of impacted hosts/instances, synthetic check ids that overlap, and K8s events for pods in that service.
2) Run the PromQL/Datadog quick probes above. If missing_points_ratio > 0.2 OR cardinality_delta < -0.3 -> mark incident as "likely telemetry loss" and follow telemetry-loss subflow.
3) Telemetry-loss subflow: check exporter logs for OOM / restart / 429s; check scrape manager logs for errors; check metric-rollup-lambda and prometheus remote-write errors for backpressure; check network egress spikes for bursts.
4) If none of the above and histogram_bucket_delta indicates bucket collapse -> mark as "aggregation bug" and escalate to instrumentation team.
5) If synthetic checks fail with matching timestamps and pod-level request latencies are unaffected -> treat synthetic as source (flaky test) and file follow-up to telemetry QA.

Notes to self / unresolved questions:
- How much suppression is acceptable from a product risk view? We need SRE + Product agreement on suppression SLAs.
- We currently lack a durable store of per-alert fingerprint vectors. Implementation idea: small Elastic index keyed by alert fingerprint hash.
- Is there value in forcing exporters to emit a heartbeat metric with a small label set to make missing-series detection simpler? This could reduce cardinality complexity.

Longer-term fixes and roadmap items:
- Instrumented alert payloads: include computed telemetry-health flags (missing_points_ratio, cardinality_delta, export_errors) so downstream MTOs can programmatically decide suppression.
- Rolling histogram sanity checks in ingestion pipeline to detect and auto-repair bucket misalignment after restarts.
- Improve upstream SDKs to attach stable series identifiers for high-cardinality flows (avoid churn that confuses rollups).
- Bake these heuristics into Redwood Console: surface telemetry-health alongside SLO dashboards.

Example incident note (real-world style):
- Incident: api-gateway p95 spike, 2026-02-27 03:11-03:19 UTC
- Symptoms: SLO alert + synthetic check fail.
- Quick probes: missing_points_ratio=0.7, cardinality_delta=-0.62, exporter-restarts=3 in same window.
- Action taken: applied 10m suppression (auto rule), pager silence note sent, restart investigation on exporter -> discovered race in exporter restart handler leading to zeroed histogram buckets.
- Follow-ups: instrumentation fix (PR 291), add exporter heartbeat metric, schedule experiment A for api-gateway.

Appendix: sample suppression pseudo-rule to discuss with Product (DSL):
- WHEN alert.type == "slo_burn" AND telemetry.missing_points_ratio > 0.3 AND telemetry.cardinality_delta < -0.5 THEN suppress_for(10m) AND notify_oncall_with_reason("telemetry_loss_suppressed")

Next actions this sprint (owners):
- Priya: spin up the fingerprint index prototype and bulk-import last 6 months of SLO alerts. (ETA: 2026-03-20)
- Ethan: implement quick_probe queries as dashboards and alert enrichment in Datadog. (ETA: 2026-03-15)
- Lina: craft product-facing doc on suppression policy and risk tradeoffs. (ETA: 2026-03-18)
- Marco: prototype exporter heartbeat in staging for two microservices and measure missing_points_ratio delta. (ETA: 2026-03-25)

If you're reading this while oncall: use the Investigation playbook above, document every step in the alert thread, and tag the incident with a fingerprint: "telemetry_loss_V1" if heuristics match. If unsure, escalate to eng-sre lead.

End of note.
